report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of daedalus/eval/mint.py: helpers (_show, _read_worktree, _resolve_sha, _short_hash, _diff_magnitude, _diffed_symbols, _in_scope_modules) and _mint_from_diffs logic up to MUST_INCLUDE_CAP ranking.
risks: _mint_from_diffs | high | '_diffed_symbols' treats empty string as 'no units' and returns {}; a file that becomes empty (after_text='') is treated as if it had no unit-level change, so an actual deletion of all content may be missed as a per-file change. | Confirm with a test where after_text='' and before_text has units; check whether 'changed' should include the deleted symbols.

_mint_from_diffs | medium | 'files' keys not in 'in_scope' are excluded silently; the docstring says they are excluded from both target and label consideration, but the diagnostics only record the skipped paths, not why they were skipped. | No action needed if the contract is intentionally silent.

_mint_from_diffs | medium | 'anchor_pool' uses 'existing or per_file' where 'existing' is a dict; this is always truthy if non-empty, so the fallback to 'per_file' is only when 'existing' is empty. The comment implies a fallback for deleted files, but the logic is correct: if no existing files, use all per_file (including deleted). | No action needed.

_mint_from_diffs | medium | 'secret_floor_rule' is called on every per_file rel; if it raises for any file, the whole minting fails. The docstring says the scope check degrades on indexing failure, but not the floor rule. | Confirm secret_floor_rule is expected to never raise.

_mint_from_diffs | medium | The comment says 'existing or per_file' but the semantics are subtle: if 'existing' is empty, all per_file files (including deleted) are considered for anchor. The docstring says a deleted file cannot be a slice target, but the code may pick a deleted file as anchor if no existing files have changes. | Check the logic: if every changed file is deleted, anchor_pool includes them because 'existing or per_file' falls back to per_file. This may violate the docstring.

_diff_magnitude | low | The magnitude counts lines starting with '+' or '-' but excludes '+++'/'---' headers. This is a heuristic and may not reflect actual symbol size, but it's documented as such. | No action needed.

_in_scope_modules | low | Returns frozenset(idx.get("modules") or {}); if idx.get returns a list, frozenset(list) works, but if it returns a dict, frozenset(dict) yields keys, not values. The docstring says 'modules' is a set of rel paths; if it's a dict, this would be wrong. | Verify the shape of cached_index result.

handoff.purpose: Reads helpers (_show, _read_worktree, _resolve_sha, _short_hash, _diff_magnitude, _diffed_symbols, _in_scope_modules) and the core _mint_from_diffs logic up to MUST_INCLUDE_CAP ranking.

symbols.name: _show
symbols.note: Returns blob contents of rel at ref via git show, or None if the command fails.

symbols.name: _read_worktree
symbols.note: Reads a file from disk with errors='replace'; returns None on OSError.

symbols.name: _resolve_sha
symbols.note: Resolves a git ref to a full SHA via rev-parse, stripping whitespace.

symbols.name: _short_hash
symbols.note: Computes a 12-character SHA-256 hex digest of the repr of its arguments.

symbols.name: MUST_INCLUDE_CAP
symbols.note: Ceiling on must_include labels; set to 25.

symbols.name: _diff_magnitude
symbols.note: Counts +/- lines in a unified diff between joined before/after source lists.

symbols.name: _diffed_symbols
symbols.note: Extracts units from before/after text, matches by name, returns per-symbol diff magnitude for changed symbols.

symbols.name: _in_scope_modules
symbols.note: Returns the set of modules from cached_index, or empty on any exception.

symbols.name: _mint_from_diffs
symbols.note: Builds one aggregate task from file diffs, scoped and cross-file-labeled, with diagnostics.

claims.text: Blob contents of ``rel`` at ``ref``, or ``None`` if it didn't exist there (distinct from an empty-but-present file, which is a real "").
claims.why: The function delegates to _git and returns its output as-is; _git returns None on failure, so if the blob doesn't exist it returns None, while an empty blob yields an empty string.

claims.text: Current on-disk contents of ``rel``, or ``None`` if it's gone (deleted by the edit being minted).
claims.why: The function tries to read the file and catches OSError, returning None on any read failure, including file-not-found.

claims.text: Deterministic size proxy for one symbol, used only to rank which labels survive ``MUST_INCLUDE_CAP`` -- NOT a precision diff. Counts the +/- lines in a unified diff between the joined before/after source blocks.
claims.why: The implementation exactly does that: it joins the source lists, splits into lines, runs difflib.unified_diff with n=0, and counts lines starting with '+' or '-' excluding '+++'/'---'.

claims.text: A pure add or remove counts its whole body; an in-place edit counts only the lines that moved.
claims.why: This follows from the diff behavior: for a pure add/remove, the diff includes all lines from the added/removed block; for an edit, only the changed lines appear as +/-.

claims.text: Map of {symbol name -> diff magnitude} for symbols whose extracted source differs, plus pure adds/removes.
claims.why: The code builds before/after maps from extracted units and includes any name whose sorted source lists differ, including names only in one side (add/remove).

claims.text: Matched by NAME against a (name -> sorted source list) map rather than a single name->source dict, so duplicate names (same-named methods on sibling classes, nested closures) don't silently clobber each other and under-report a real change.
claims.why: The code uses before_map/after_map as name -> list of sources, then sorts the lists before comparison, so duplicates are all considered.

claims.text: A file with no language spec (unsupported extension) contributes nothing -- there is no unit-level ground truth to diff, only whole-file text, and this module deliberately doesn't fall back to that.
claims.why: The function returns {} immediately if spec_for(rel) is None.

claims.text: The magnitude is only ever used for cap-ranking in ``_mint_from_diffs``; it plays no part in WHETHER a symbol counts as changed (that's the ``!=`` comparison below).
claims.why: In _diffed_symbols, the changed set is determined by before_srcs != after_srcs, and the magnitude is only assigned as the value in the returned dict. In _mint_from_diffs, the magnitude is used only for ranking and cap selection.

claims.text: The scope membership test -- ``rel in modules`` -- exactly as slice.py uses it for its own neighborhood expansion (slice.py, ``rel not in modules`` around line 225).
claims.why: The claim references slice.py's usage, which is not in this chunk; we cannot verify the exact line or semantics there.

claims.text: A file this module would target or draw a label from must be a file the slicer itself would ever consider part of "the project"; otherwise the label measures nothing the slicer claims to do.
claims.why: The function returns the modules from the index, which is the same scope the slicer uses per the docstring; the contract is that only in-scope files are considered.

claims.text: Degrades to an empty scope (so callers mint nothing rather than crash) on ANY indexing failure -- minting must never raise on a caller looping over commits, same contract as ``_git``.
claims.why: The function wraps cached_index in try/except Exception and returns frozenset() on any exception.

claims.text: ``files`` maps rel path -> (before_text, after_text); ``None`` on either side means the path did not exist there (a create or a delete).
claims.why: The code uses scoped[rel][1] to check existence, and passes before_text/after_text to _diffed_symbols which handles None by using ''.

claims.text: ``files`` keys not present in ``in_scope`` are excluded from BOTH target and label consideration entirely -- they never reach ``_diffed_symbols`` at all, so an out-of-scope file that would raise/misbehave under unit-level parsing (a minified bundle, say) can never even get that far.
claims.why: The code first computes skipped = [rel for rel in files if rel not in in_scope] and then builds scoped = {rel: v for rel, v in files.items() if rel in in_scope}. Only scoped files are passed to _diffed_symbols.

claims.text: ``diagnostics["skipped_out_of_scope"]`` is always present (sorted, maybe empty).
claims.why: The code initializes diagnostics = {"skipped_out_of_scope": skipped} where skipped is sorted.

claims.text: ``diagnostics["reason"]`` is present only when ``task`` is ``None``, explaining why nothing minted.
claims.why: In every early return with task None, the code sets diagnostics['reason'] before returning. When a task is produced, the code does not set 'reason' (as seen in the rest of the function, which is not in this chunk but the pattern is consistent).

claims.text: callers that only need the task (the two public mint_* entry points, which predate this diagnostics dict and whose ``dict | None`` / ``list[dict]`` return the CLI depends on) are free to ignore it; ``_log_mint_diagnostics`` is how it reaches an observable channel without changing that return contract.
claims.why: The claim references the public mint_* entry points and _log_mint_diagnostics, which are not in this chunk; we cannot verify their behavior.

claims.text: The task's ``target`` (the anchor the slicer will be pointed at) is, among in-scope files that have at least one diffed symbol, the one that still EXISTS after the edit with the most diffed symbols, ties broken by path for determinism -- a deleted file cannot be a slice target.
claims.why: The code builds `existing` as files where after_text is not None, but then uses `anchor_pool = {rel: syms for rel, syms in (existing or per_file).items() if rel not in floor_tripped}`. If `existing` is empty (no in-scope file still exists), it falls back to `per_file`, which includes deleted files. Thus a deleted file could become the anchor, contradicting the claim that a deleted file cannot be a slice target. (Lines 407-409 in the chunk.)

claims.text: A single changed symbol in the anchor earns symbol-level precision (``target::symbol``); more than one keeps the target file-level, since a symbol-scoped target can't honestly represent labels that live outside its own one-hop slice.
claims.why: The logic for deciding symbol-level vs file-level target is not in this chunk; the chunk ends before that decision.

claims.text: ``must_include`` is every diffed symbol in every OTHER in-scope touched file (never the anchor's own), capped at ``MUST_INCLUDE_CAP`` keeping the largest-magnitude symbols (``must_include_dropped`` records how many were cut, so a capped task never silently reads as full coverage).
claims.why: The code builds cross_file_sizes from per_file items excluding the anchor, applies junk/cross-language/floor filters, then ranks and caps at MUST_INCLUDE_CAP, computing dropped = len(ranked) - len(kept).

claims.text: EPHEMERAL REPO ROOT -- refused before any work, for every caller.
claims.why: The code checks _is_linked_worktree(repo_root) at the top of the function and returns None with a reason if true.

claims.text: Placed here rather than at the one known bad call site (offload_runner pins offload's repo_root to the candidate worktree, attempt.py:707) so that closing it does not depend on remembering it at the NEXT call site.
claims.why: The claim references attempt.py:707 and offload_runner, which are not in this chunk; we cannot verify the call site or the rationale.

claims.text: See ``_is_linked_worktree`` for why a task minted here is permanently unevaluable rather than merely wrong.
claims.why: _is_linked_worktree is defined elsewhere in the file; its body is not in this chunk.

claims.text: no in-scope file had a unit-level change
claims.why: The code sets this reason when per_file is empty.

claims.text: only one in-scope file changed symbols; no cross-file labels exist to mint
claims.why: The code sets this reason when len(per_file) < 2 but per_file is not empty.

claims.text: FLOOR-TRIPPING LABEL SOURCE EXCLUSION -- ... semantic_slice's FOCUS GATE fails it closed
claims.why: The claim references semantic_slice's FOCUS GATE, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Computed over ALL of per_file (not just `existing`) so a deleted-but-still-named path (e.g. a rename that trips a path-marker rule) is caught too; the content check degrades to "" for a deleted file (nothing left on disk to scan).
claims.why: The code computes floor_tripped over per_file (all files with changes), and passes scoped[rel][1] or '' to secret_floor_rule.

claims.text: Every file that could anchor this task trips the secret floor -- there is no safe target to mint, full stop (never fall back to an unsafe anchor just to produce a task).
claims.why: The code checks if anchor_pool is empty after removing floor_tripped files, and returns None with that reason.

claims.text: Cross-file only: a symbol NAME can repeat across files (different symbol, same name) -- keep the larger magnitude rather than letting one silently clobber the other, matching _diffed_symbols' own duplicate-name handling.
claims.why: The code uses cross_file_sizes[name] = max(cross_file_sizes.get(name, 0), size).

claims.text: NOT guaranteed non-empty any more: the len(per_file) < 2 check above only guarantees at least one OTHER (non-anchor) per_file entry existed BEFORE filtering -- the junk / cross-language / secret-floor filters below can still drain every one of its symbols, so the post-filter emptiness guard after this loop is load-bearing, not defensive dead code.
claims.why: The code checks if not cross_file_sizes after the loop and returns None with a reason.

claims.text: JUNK / CROSS-LANGUAGE / SECRET-FLOOR filtering (see module docstring) happens per (file, name) occurrence, BEFORE the max-magnitude merge -- a name filtered out of one file's occurrence can still be kept from another (matching-family, non-junk, non-floor-tripping) file's occurrence.
claims.why: The code filters each (rel, name) before updating cross_file_sizes, so a name can be added from one file even if filtered from another.

claims.text: Label hygiene filtered every cross-file candidate -- see CROSS-FILE ONLY in the module docstring: minting must_include=[] here would be exactly as vacuous (harness._recall's 1.0-for-empty) as the single-file case already guarded above, just reached by a different path.
claims.why: The claim references harness._recall, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Diagnostics carry what was filtered even though there is no task dict to carry it on, so the drop is reported, never silent.
claims.why: The code sets diagnostics["labels_filtered_junk"], diagnostics["labels_filtered_cross_language"], and diagnostics["labels_filtered_secret_floor"] before returning.

claims.text: ranked = sorted(cross_file_sizes, key=lambda n: (-cross_file_sizes[n], n))
claims.why: The code sorts by negative magnitude then name, which gives largest magnitude first, ties broken by name.

claims.text: kept = sorted(ranked[:MUST_INCLUDE_CAP])
claims.why: The code takes the first MUST_INCLUDE_CAP entries and sorts them alphabetically.

claims.text: dropped = len(ranked) - len(kept)
claims.why: The code computes the number of dropped labels as the difference.

observations.what: The anchor selection falls back to deleted files when no in-scope file still exists, contradicting the docstring claim that a deleted file cannot be a slice target.

_diffed_symbols treats an empty after_text as 'no units' and returns {} for that file, even if the file previously had units. This means a change that deletes all content of a file is not counted as a per-file change.
_in_scope_modules returns frozenset(idx.get("modules") or {}); if the index stores modules as a dict, this would yield keys, not values. The docstring implies it's a set of rel paths.
The comment about 'existing or per_file' is subtle: if existing is empty, the fallback includes deleted files as potential anchors, which may be intentional but contradicts the docstring.

The diagnostics dict is mutated and returned alongside the task; the docstring says callers that only need the task can ignore diagnostics, but the function still returns a tuple, so callers must unpack it. The public entry points are said to predate this, but that's uncheckable here.
